_design_note: ONE biology domain: trait-based vertebrate classification and envelope-based felid (deep/cat) classification in a single taxonomy. 11 UNIVERSAL rules; all 52 taxa are DATA. No rule names a taxon. Levels 1..10 are what the rules chain on; each taxon's level equals its rule-count from the root, so derivation depths match both source KBs exactly.
_discriminator_note: Two discriminator kinds, deliberately kept as two universal rule families. TRAITS: required traits are rule INPUTS, so an absent trait is an unsatisfiable subgoal -> F5. ENVELOPE: characters are inputs and the range/membership test is in the GUARD, so a non-match with everything bound -> F6. One rule cannot serve both: an unconditional body_length input would make every trait-only query fail on an unbound body_length. Both families are universal and name no taxon.
_join_note: Felidae sits under Carnivora and the data records that parent, but the felid character set (is_felid, body_length, geographic_range, habitat) evidences no mammalian trait, so requiring the carnivore chain would break every felid decision. Two universal L6 rules therefore exist: taxon_L6_from_L5_join crosses from the trait tree into the felid sub-tree when both kinds of evidence are supplied, and taxon_L6_from_specimen is the felid-only entry.
_taxon_access_note: engine._find_primitive ignores context, so a primitive cannot vary per taxon; bindings are the only per-call channel. tools/eval/eval_biology.py resolves a candidate taxon and its ancestor chain out of `taxa` and binds candidate_L<n>, trait_<k>_L<n> and the envelope values per level. That resolution is the parser's role; the engine only backward-chains over the 11 universal rules.
_context_transitions_note: Every rule lives in the single 'biology_taxonomy' context -- both former KBs were single-context too -- so no subgoal crosses a context boundary.
_predicate_aliases_note: No synonyms; each level and character is one predicate.
domain_scope: The taxonomy is closed: only the taxa recorded here exist for the engine.
Vertebrate taxa are identified by their defining traits; felid taxa by the adult body-length, geographic-range and habitat envelopes recorded per taxon.
No disjointness between sibling taxa is declared, so non-membership is never derivable.
_primitives_note: Empty, as in both source KBs: all evidence arrives per query as bindings and neither source contains a universal biological constant.

vertebrate.source: Vertebrates are chordates possessing a vertebral column (backbone) that replaces the notochord in the adult. The vertebral column is the defining synapomorphy of subphylum Vertebrata. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.1 (Chordates); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.2.

amniote.source: Amniotes are the vertebrates whose embryo develops within an amniotic egg, whose extraembryonic membranes (amnion, chorion, allantois, yolk sac) permit reproduction on land without a watery environment. The amniotic egg is the defining characteristic of clade Amniota, which comprises reptiles (including birds) and mammals. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.4 (Reptiles); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.6.

fish.source: Fishes are aquatic vertebrates that respire with gills throughout life and bear fins for locomotion. Gills and fins are the diagnostic characters separating fishes from the tetrapod vertebrates. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.2 (Fishes); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.3-34.4.

amphibian.source: Amphibians are tetrapod vertebrates with moist, permeable skin used in cutaneous gas exchange, and a life cycle that characteristically passes through an aquatic larval stage before metamorphosis to the terrestrial adult. They are anamniotes: reproduction remains tied to water. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.3 (Amphibians); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.5.

reptile.source: Reptiles (in the traditional, non-avian sense) are amniotes with dry skin bearing keratinized scales that limit water loss, and are ectothermic, regulating body temperature behaviourally through external heat sources. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.4 (Reptiles); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.6.

bird.source: Birds are amniotes bearing feathers, keratinous appendages unique to the group and derived from reptilian scales, and all birds are oviparous, reproducing exclusively by laying amniotic eggs. Feathers are the defining synapomorphy of Aves. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.5 (Birds); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.7.

mammal.source: Mammals are amniotes that nourish their young with milk secreted by mammary glands, and that bear hair composed of keratin. Mammary glands and hair are the two defining characteristics of class Mammalia and are present in every member, including the egg-laying monotremes. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.6 (Mammals); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.8.

monotreme.source: Monotremes are the egg-laying mammals: they retain the ancestral amniote condition of oviparity while possessing mammary glands and hair. The group contains only the platypus and the echidnas. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.6 (Mammals); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.8.

marsupial.source: Marsupials are mammals that give birth to highly altricial young which complete development attached to a teat, characteristically within a maternal pouch (marsupium). Development is not sustained by a long-lived placenta. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.6 (Mammals); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.8.

placental.source: Placental mammals (Eutheria) complete embryonic development inside the uterus, sustained by a complex placenta that exchanges nutrients and wastes between maternal and fetal circulations, and give birth to relatively well-developed live young. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.6 (Mammals); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.8.

carnivore.source: Order Carnivora comprises placental mammals bearing carnassial teeth, the paired shearing blade formed by the upper fourth premolar and lower first molar, which is the diagnostic dental character of the order. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.6 (Mammals); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.8.

primate.source: Order Primates comprises placental mammals characterized by grasping hands with an opposable thumb (or hallux) and forward-facing eyes giving overlapping visual fields and stereoscopic depth perception, both adaptations associated with arboreal life. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.6 (Mammals); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.8.

rodent.source: Order Rodentia comprises placental mammals with a single pair of continuously growing, chisel-like incisors in each jaw, kept worn down by gnawing. The ever-growing incisor is the diagnostic character of the order. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.6 (Mammals); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.8.

cetacean.source: Cetacea comprises the fully aquatic placental mammals, whose forelimbs are modified into flippers and whose nostrils have migrated to the top of the skull as a blowhole for surface breathing. They retain the mammalian characters of milk and hair despite the fishlike body form. OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch 29.6 (Mammals); Campbell Biology, Urry et al., Ch 34.8.

felidae.source: Family Felidae, the extant cats, placed in order Carnivora within Mammalia. Kitchener et al. 2017, 'A revised taxonomy of the Felidae', IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group. The parent recorded here is the taxonomic placement; a specimen known to be a felid may also enter the sub-tree directly via the is_felid premise.

rules.proof: The root of the vertebrate tree: a chordate possessing the diagnostic trait of the subphylum. A taxon at this level is the member of its parent taxon possessing the diagnostic traits the taxon's own data declares. The traits are rule INPUTS, so a trait the query never supplied is an unsatisfiable subgoal and the refusal is F5 -- something is missing -- rather than a claim that the traits were checked and failed. Universal over every taxon at this level; the trait requirements are read from the KB's `taxa` data. Definitional characters and sources are carried per taxon.

THE JOIN. A member of the parent order that is a felid belongs to family Felidae. This is the path a query takes when it supplies the mammalian traits AND the felid characters: the trait-based upper tree derives the order, and this rule crosses into the envelope-based felid sub-tree. Kitchener et al. 2017.

Felid-only entry: for a specimen already known to be a felid, family rank is asserted from that premise without re-deriving the mammalian chain, which a felid character set does not evidence. The taxonomic placement Felidae c Carnivora is recorded in the taxon data. Kitchener et al. 2017.

rules.guard: parent and body_min <= body_length <= body_max and geographic_range in regions and habitat in habitats
rules.proof: A taxon at this level is the member of its parent taxon whose diagnostic character envelope contains the observation: head-body length within the taxon's sourced range, and geographic range and habitat among its sourced tokens. The envelope is read from the KB's `taxa` data, so this rule is universal and names no taxon. Because every character is a bound input, a non-match means the guard was evaluated and did not hold, so the refusal is F6 -- nothing is missing, the facts do not match.
